race.name: The River
race.tagline: 160 km of Ardennes forest gravel along the Semois, raced as a round of The Traka World Series.

vitals.course_status: 2027 Queen Race track, feed zones and cutoffs published
vitals.field_size: About 1,000 riders across four distances in 2026; 2027 cap not published
vitals.start_time: Queen Race 160: Saturday 7:30 from the event village on Rue de la Poulie
vitals.registration: Opens soon; 2027 prices not yet published
vitals.prize_purse: EUR 8,000 per Traka World Series round
vitals.aid_stations: Feed and assistance zones at km 43.7 (Chassepierre/Breux), km 98.8 (Epioux, life bag) and km 131.5 (Auby), plus the finish

climate.description: The 2026 edition started in fog in the Semois valley, then the sun came through for near-ideal racing temperatures.
challenges: Changeable autumn weather in the Ardennes

terrain.primary: Ardennes forest tracks and riverside gravel
terrain.surface: The Queen Race track is 72% unpaved and 28% paved: fast forest tracks, rolling climbs and riverside gravel along the Semois, with 38-45 mm tires recommended. The course never rises above 440 m, so its 2,550 m of gain comes from repeated short climbs rather than one long one.
features: 2,550 m of gain from repeated climbs

gravel_god_rating.score_note: The River lands in Tier 2 on 2,550 m of Ardennes climbing, professional race-day support and a pro field deep enough to settle the 2026 series titles. It stays below Tier 1 because it has one edition of history and its 100-mile Queen Race is long but not ultra.

biased_opinion.summary: The River hides its climbing in repetition: 160 km, 2,550 m of gain, and a high point of just 440 m. It ran for the first time in 2026 as the Gravel Earth Series finale, where the men's and women's winners clinched the overall titles, and returns in 2027 as a round of The Traka World Series. The production is already professional. What it lacks is history.
strengths: Round 6 of The Traka World Series
Published feed zones, assistance areas and cutoffs
Fast forest and riverside gravel along the Semois
weaknesses: No long climb to settle into
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Go for the forest gravel and the pro race up front, and pace it like a climbing day: the 2,550 m arrives in small pieces.

final_verdict.one_liner: 160 km of Semois forest gravel where 2,550 m of climbing arrives in small pieces.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a fast, well-run European race with a pro field and a 10-hour cutoff that most riders can make. Wait if you want a race with a long track record.
final_verdict.alternatives: For the full Traka experience, race The Traka in Girona.

logistics.airport: Luxembourg (LUX) and Brussels (BRU) are the nearest major airports; plan on a car to reach Bouillon.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in Bouillon to walk to the event village, and book early in a small town.
logistics.food: On course, feed zones sit at km 43.7, 98.8 and 131.5, with a life bag at Epioux.

history.origin_story: The River grew out of the GRG Gravel, part of Bouillon's Grand Raid Godefroy program since 2023. Klassmark made it the 2026 Gravel Earth Series finale and stretched the top distance from 110 km to 160 km.
notable_moments: 2026: first edition, about 1,000 riders, and the Gravel Earth Series finale
2026: Mads Würtz Schmidt won the Queen Race in 4:36:43 and Geerike Schreurs won the women's race in 5:23:13; both clinched the series titles
2027: round 6 of The Traka World Series
history.reputation: A young, fast Ardennes race with Klassmark production.

course_description.character: The 2027 Queen Race runs 160.2 km from Bouillon's event village with 2,550 m of gain, 72% of it unpaved. Fast forest tracks, rolling climbs and riverside gravel follow the Semois, and the course never climbs above 440 m.

suffering_zones.label: First Cutoff
suffering_zones.desc: Feed Zone 1 closes at 10:10, two hours and forty minutes after the start.

suffering_zones.label: Life-Bag Stop
suffering_zones.desc: Feed Zone 2 holds your life bag and closes at 13:48.

suffering_zones.label: Last Feed
suffering_zones.desc: The final feed before Bouillon closes at 15:48.

course_description.signature_challenge: Keeping 2,550 m of short, repeated climbs from turning a fast race into a slow finish.

guide_variables.race_distance: 160.2 km / 99.5 miles (Queen Race); 120 and 70 km also offered
guide_variables.race_terrain: Ardennes forest tracks, riverside gravel and village roads; 72% unpaved
guide_variables.race_weather: Cool September start in the Semois valley

migration_notes: 2026-11-05: Added as a new profile after The Traka World Series named The River round 6 for 2027. Organizer publishes the September 11, 2027 date and the 160.2 km / 2,550 m Queen Race track; prices are not yet published. The 2026 edition also offered a 220 km ultra, which the 2027 site mentions but does not yet publish as a track.

logistics.explanation: Moderate planning. Race day is tidy, with one event village in Bouillon and three assistance zones on course [2]; reaching a small Ardennes town is the work.

length.explanation: Long, not ultra. The Queen Race is 160.2 km, about 99.5 miles [2], with 120 and 70 km options below it [1].

technicality.explanation: Fast more than technical. The track is 72% unpaved forest and riverside gravel with 38-45 mm tires recommended [2], and the 2026 winner averaged 34.7 km/h [5].

elevation.explanation: The climbing adds up. 2,550 m (8,366 ft) of gain [2] comes from repeated short ascents rather than one big climb [5].

climate.explanation: Mostly kind. The 2026 edition started in cool valley fog that gave way to near-ideal racing temperatures [5].

altitude.explanation: Irrelevant. The course stays between 212 m and 440 m [2].

adventure.explanation: Destination-worthy. The route follows the Semois through Ardennes forests and valleys [5], with the base camp on the riverbank [6].

prestige.explanation: New, with serious backing. The 2026 edition was the first and closed the Gravel Earth Series season [5], and 2027 makes it round 6 of The Traka World Series [4].

race_quality.explanation: Professional from the first edition. The Queen Race publishes feed zones, assistance areas, a life-bag drop and every cutoff [2], and The Traka's organizer Klassmark co-runs it [5].

experience.explanation: Enjoyable, not yet mythic. A dawn start in the Semois fog [5] and a single-village start and finish [2] make a good day, but one edition is not a legend.

community.explanation: A solid start. About 1,000 riders took on four distances in 2026 [5], on top of a local gravel scene the GRG Gravel had been building since 2023 [6].

field_depth.explanation: Strong pro racing. Mads Würtz Schmidt won 2026 in 4:36:43 ahead of Célestin Guillon, and Geerike Schreurs took the women's race by more than five minutes [5].

value.explanation: Fair, pending a price. 2027 fees are not out yet [1], against a well-supported race with three feed zones and a 10-hour cutoff [2].

expenses.explanation: Moderate. Fees are not out yet [1]; for most riders the real cost is travel and lodging in a small Ardennes town.
